quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour.
Never.

questions.explanation: Never block an intersection. Even if the light is green, only enter if you can cross completely before it turns red. You can be fined for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: How should you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Stop immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with its siren on and lights flashing. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can go again after it passes.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed constant.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down in wet weather to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: Held safely by a strong adult.
Standing on the floor in the back.
They are safe in accidents because they are small.
Always properly restrained in a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always properly restrained in a seat.
questions.explanation: Children must always be properly restrained in a seat. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident. Use a child safety seat designed for the child's size.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back in these conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: How far ahead should you signal before turning?

options.text: 50 feet
100 feet
150 feet

questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn. This gives other drivers time to see and react to your signal.

questions.question: What should you do if a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look at their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside it.
Let it share half a lane with you.
Pass it using the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs a full lane width. It needs room to maneuver safely. Treat it as a full-size vehicle with the same road privileges.

questions.question: What should you use to see better in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help others see you better. High beams create glare in these conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road.
Pavement ends.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.question: When steering a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel on the outside.
Use a firm but gentle grip. Use your fingers, not your palms.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel with thumbs pointing up. Grip gently but firmly with your fingers, not your palms. Turn the wheel by gripping the outside, not the inside.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When you see an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never drive to an accident just to look.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and gradually return to the road when it is safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gradually return to the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road right away. Reduce your speed, check for traffic, and gradually turn back when it is safe.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive in the same lane as a motorcycle.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there seems to be room. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to stay safe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must be aware of:

options.text: Vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks with hazardous materials.
Multiple trains coming from either direction.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only with large vehicles.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, and when behind a motorcycle or bicycle. Also increase it if someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When driving near cyclists, you should:

options.text: Treat bicycles as vehicles on the road.
Be extra careful when driving near cyclists.
Leave plenty of space when turning after passing a cyclist.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars. Drive carefully near cyclists and keep a safe distance. When you turn after passing a cyclist, leave plenty of room so you do not cut them off.

questions.question: At many intersections, you can turn right when the traffic light is red. What must you do before turning right on red?

options.text: Slow down and go if the way is clear. You do not need to stop.
Stop completely, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
Speed up because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, you can turn right at a red light. You must stop completely before the crosswalk. Let all pedestrians and cross traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: Which statement about left turns is correct?

options.text: Swing wide into the right lane when turning left.
You cannot turn left on red from a two-way street.
When turning left onto a four-lane street, finish the turn in the far right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn left on red from a two-way street.
questions.explanation: You can only turn left on red when you turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street. Always finish a left turn in the lane closest to your starting lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
The road ahead has many turns and curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about possible dangers. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet. Drive carefully in wet conditions.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
As soon as you pass the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough space to safely get back in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front of them?

options.text: To let other drivers merge onto the freeway.
So the truck can stop safely.
To help other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck can stop safely.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger than cars and need more time to stop at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They get you ready for hazards ahead. This sign warns you that there is a sharp turn coming. Slow down.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean about passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When the center line has a solid yellow line on one side and a broken yellow line on the other, you can only pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can clearly see in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad gate. After the gate is raised, wait until you can clearly see in both directions and are sure no train is coming before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: What must you do when you reach an intersection with a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic or pedestrians go, then go.
Slow down and go carefully.
Stop and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic or pedestrians go, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, let oncoming traffic or pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.
